rules.quote: Write the titles of bills in roman type, not italics.

covers.quote: Lower case is correct, unless the reference is to a specific bill
If you are writing about 2 or more bills, use the lower case: ‘the bills’, ‘these bills’.
If you write about a bill or bills generally, use the lower case: ‘a bill’, ‘some bills’.
If there’s any chance the text is unclear to readers, use a capital ‘B’.

examples.note: The plural reference is lower case; the individual titles retain their capitals.

parts.quote: The government drafted a legislative package that includes 3 bills:
the Religious Discrimination Bill 2019
the Religious Discrimination (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2019
the Human Rights Legislation Amendment (Freedom of Religion) Bill 2019.

rules.quote: Always use an initial capital for the word ‘Bill’ when you write about a specific bill: ‘the Bill’, ‘this Bill’.
rules.specification: The capital-B exception depends on a risk of reader confusion. The page gives no objective test for that risk.
rules.violation_condition: A reference to a specific individual bill uses lower-case ‘bill’, or a plural or general reference uses capitalised ‘Bill’ or ‘Bills’ without a reader-clarity reason.
when: Capitalise ‘Bill’ for a specific individual bill.
Use lower case when referring collectively to 2 or more bills.
Use lower case for bills discussed generally.
Use a capital ‘B’ if a lower-case reference could be unclear to readers.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: consolidate the specific, plural, general and clarity cases into one reference-capitalisation rule.

covers.quote: Bills contain clauses, which become sections when bills become Acts. Clauses can be divided into subclauses, then into paragraphs and then into subparagraphs.
Long bills have clauses grouped into parts, divisions and subdivisions.
Always use an initial capital for these units, for example ‘Part 1’.

parts.quote: Clause 12 vests Commonwealth powers in the Minister …

examples.note: The unit name is lower case within the sentence.

rules.quote: Use lower case for these units of a bill unless they begin a sentence.

when: Use lower case for clause, subclause, paragraph and subparagraph.
Capitalise a lower-level unit name when it begins a sentence.
Use an initial capital for Part, Division and Subdivision.
rules.why: G-2: unit level and sentence position are cases determining the capitalisation of a bill-unit name.

covers.quote: Commonwealth bills refer to units below clause level using the smallest unit of text.

rules.quote: Content that discusses the operation and effect of certain subclauses, paragraphs and subparagraphs will cite at the smallest unit level. A general discussion about the provisions of a bill will cite at clause level.
